title: EXP-038 — Hello World Part 1 — FX_ SQL Table and IDO Creation Feasibility
objective: Determine whether the current Site Developer user can create exactly one new FX_-prefixed SQL table containing two simple application columns and exactly one FX_-prefixed IDO backed by that table, using the supported Mongoose SQL Tables, IDOs, and IDO Projects forms or an appropriate documented New Data Maintenance wizard. Create one FX_-prefixed IDO project, because every new IDO must belong to one. First inspect the Hello World Part 1 instructions, authenticated application state, permissions, available UI controls, and target-name collisions without mutation. Choose one supported creation path before making changes. If prerequisites pass, create the smallest valid table-to-IDO pair, save it through the supported UI, check the new IDO in if it is left checked out, close and reopen the relevant maintenance surfaces, and verify the created definitions using rendered evidence. Stop at the first permission, wizard, metadata, or unexpected-object error. Do not build any Form, generate business records, or perform deployment. Record every object created for eventual operator-controlled cleanup.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt1.md, transcripts/raw/raw-hello-world-pt1.txt, and relevant existing recipes before browser mutation. Resolve exact tutorial terminology and supported creation steps.
Read-only preflight of the authenticated Web Client, current configuration, Site Developer permissions where visible, and User editing scope where applicable.
Read-only inspection of supported SQL Tables, IDOs, and IDO Projects maintenance forms and their actual creation controls.
Read-only inspection of the New Data Maintenance wizard only if it is an appropriate documented alternative capable of creating the specified table and IDO without generating a Form.

Check that FX_HelloWorldData01, FX_HelloWorldIDO01, FX_HelloWorldProject01 and the fallback project name FXHelloWorld01 do not already exist, using supported visible inventories before any mutation. Stop on collision or unverifiable identity.
Choose one supported creation route before mutation. Prefer the tutorial's core SQL Tables and IDO maintenance forms when available. Do not switch routes after a failed creation attempt.

Create at most one SQL table named FX_HelloWorldData01 with application columns FX_Code as a string of length 30 and FX_Label as a string of length 100, or equivalent supported string types. Permit only system columns, keys, or metadata required by the supported Mongoose creation procedure. Document all automatically generated columns.
Create at most one IDO named FX_HelloWorldIDO01 backed by FX_HelloWorldData01. Verify the base-table relationship and the two application-column mappings or properties through the supported UI.

Create exactly one IDO project for the new IDO: every new IDO must belong to an IDO project (specialist, documented) and no existing non-FX_ project may be used. Use the name FX_HelloWorldProject01. Only if the IDO Projects form visibly rejects that name (for example an alphanumeric-only rule) before any record is saved, use the fallback FXHelloWorld01 once, record the exact rejection message, and record the fallback as an operator-authorized naming exception. Do not change membership or definitions of existing non-FX_ projects.

Object prefix (specialist, documented): Mongoose can enforce an Access As / object prefix (cloud tenants often use ue_) on new tables and IDOs. In T1, inspect the creation surfaces for an enforced or pre-filled prefix. If one is enforced, stop before mutation and report the prefix and the resulting names; the operator decides the names.

Table options: leave Multi-Site cleared (no SiteRef, no generated views). Record which system columns and triggers SQL Tables generates automatically (e.g. CreateDate, CreatedBy); these are expected side effects, not unrelated objects.

IDO check-in (specialist, documented): the IDO Wizard may leave the new IDO checked out. If FX_HelloWorldIDO01 is checked out after creation, check it in once through the supported Check In action of the IDOs or IDO Projects form, and record the check-out/check-in state before and after. Check in nothing else.

Use the supported ordinary Save or wizard completion operations required to commit the new objects. Record exact operation counts, visible success or failure messages, and available captured responses.

Close and reopen the relevant maintenance Form or object-selection surface after saving, and verify the table definition, column definitions, IDO identity, base-table relationship, and optional project association.

Capture decisive screenshots and accessibility snapshots identifying each object, its creation surface, the resulting values, and the post-reopen state. Distinguish visible UI evidence from backend persistence claims.
Record every created SQL table, IDO, IDO project, and automatically generated dependency in evidence/EXP-038/ for later cleanup. Do not perform cleanup during this experiment.
Update only the EXP-038 experiment record and evidence/EXP-038/. Preserve existing recipes, other experiments, and factory configuration.
out_of_scope: Creating or modifying Mongoose Forms, including the Hello World data-maintenance Form.
Adding Form components, Form events, handlers, variables, scripts, or validation logic.
Creating, inserting, updating, or deleting application data records.
Testing IDO runtime CRUD operations, custom methods, or application business logic.
Using existing non-FX_ SQL tables, IDOs, or IDO projects as mutation targets.
Creating additional business columns, relationships, foreign keys, triggers, indexes, or procedures beyond the minimum required by the supported creation process.
FormSync, application deployment, publication, or synchronization between configurations.
Explicit metadata-cache unloading, Form regeneration, or cache-clearing experiments.
Direct SQL execution, direct database access, internal endpoints, reverse-engineered client stores, or unsupported API calls.
Changing user permissions, tenant security, authentication configuration, or editing-scope preferences.
Testing alternative creation mechanisms after the first permission, wizard, or creation failure.
Automatic deletion or cleanup of created artifacts.
Claims about independent database durability, cache eviction, or replay verification.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values
Never create or modify a non-FX_-prefixed SQL table, IDO, project, Form, or other Mongoose artifact.
Never alter the schema, membership, permissions, or configuration of an existing non-FX_ object.
Never create more than one experimental table, one experimental IDO, or one experimental IDO project.
Never allow a wizard to generate a Form, application data records, or other unrelated objects.
Never proceed if the wizard's full object-creation scope cannot be determined before its final commit.
Never bypass disabled controls, permission failures, metadata errors, or an unavailable supported UI by using scripts, direct URLs, hidden controls, or internal APIs.

Never retry an uncertain creation, Save, Finish, or other potentially state-changing operation without first establishing that no object was created. If the required recovery would exceed the allowed budget, stop.
Never switch from the chosen core-form or wizard creation route to another route after the first creation failure.
Never perform FormSync, deployment, publication, cache unload, Regenerate, or direct SQL execution.
Never change tenant permissions, security roles, credentials, or user preferences.
Never deliberately reauthenticate or replace the active session during the experiment. Stop if an authentication or session-establishment prompt blocks the required operation.
Never create or modify application data records.
Never delete experimental objects as an unapproved cleanup operation.
Never exceed one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Stop and document a blocker when either required recovery exceeds its allowance.
Never infer successful creation solely from a click, a success toast, a filename, or the presence of an unsaved editor. Require object-specific postconditions and supported readback.
Never check in, check out, or change the source-control state of any object other than FX_HelloWorldIDO01.

acceptance_checks.description: Repository evidence identifies the exact applicable Hello World Part 1 SQL-table and IDO workflow, the AGENTS.md authorization, and any required system columns or project prerequisites. Browser evidence shows the authenticated target configuration and usable supported maintenance UI. The worker distinguishes User editing scope from the tenant-wide effects of creating SQL tables and IDOs. Capture evidence before mutation. Evidence records whether an Access As / object prefix is enforced on new tables and IDOs; if one is, the experiment stops before mutation.

Before mutation, evidence identifies the supported SQL Tables, IDOs, and IDO Projects controls or the chosen documented wizard, their visible permission and availability state, and the intended creation path. Supported inventories show no existing object with any required target name or the fallback project name FXHelloWorld01, including case-insensitive collisions. If access, collision checks, or creation permissions cannot be established, stop before creating anything.

The supported UI confirms creation of exactly one table FX_HelloWorldData01. Its saved definition identifies the exact table name and application columns FX_Code and FX_Label with the intended string types and lengths. Any automatically required system columns are inventoried. Evidence identifies the successful commit and confirms through a supported FX_ inventory that no other new FX_ table was created. Multi-Site is cleared.

After an ordinary close and supported reopen of the relevant SQL Tables maintenance surface, FX_HelloWorldData01 can be selected again and its two application columns, types, lengths, and required system metadata match the post-creation baseline. Capture the selected object name and recovered column details together with a concise comparison.

The supported UI confirms creation of exactly one FX_HelloWorldIDO01 associated with base table FX_HelloWorldData01, with the two intended application-column properties or mappings visible, and exactly one new IDO project (FX_HelloWorldProject01, or FXHelloWorld01 only after a recorded visible rejection of the underscore name) shown as the IDO's project. The IDO's check-out/check-in state is recorded after creation and after any check-in.

After ordinary close and supported reopen of the IDO maintenance surface, the same FX_HelloWorldIDO01 is selectable and visibly retains its identity, base-table relationship, application-column properties, project association, and checked-in state (or the exact reason it could not be checked in). The UI shows a clean saved state without errors or pending changes. This establishes supported metadata readback, not independent database durability.

The final object inventory and creation-action audit reconcile exactly one FX_ SQL table, one FX_ IDO, and one FX_ IDO project (or the recorded FXHelloWorld01 fallback), together with every required automatically generated dependency. No new Form, application data record, or unrelated artifact is reported. If a permission or wizard failure stopped the experiment earlier, capture the exact failure and all objects created up to that point rather than claiming successful completion.

The final evidence matrix identifies the actual creation route, visible permissions, object identities, Save and completion counts, close/reopen checks, recovery-budget use, and exact screenshot or response paths. Repository changes are confined to the EXP-038 record and evidence/EXP-038/. No prohibited operation occurred. Findings are classified as observed only, with explicit limitations concerning runtime functionality, database durability, cache behavior, and independent replay.

initial_instruction: T1 — REPOSITORY REVIEW AND READ-ONLY FEASIBILITY PREFLIGHT ONLY. Read AGENTS.md and the Hello World Part 1 tutorial at docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt1.md, checking exact tutorial spellings against the raw transcript at transcripts/raw/raw-hello-world-pt1.txt. Identify the SQL Tables, IDOs, IDO Projects, and New Data Maintenance steps that are actually documented, together with mandatory system columns and object-creation side effects. Review the relevant previous experiment evidence. Inspect the existing browser session, authenticated configuration, supported maintenance-form availability, permissions, and exact-name collisions. Determine whether the core-form route or the documented wizard could create only the authorized FX_ table-to-IDO pair, with one FX_ IDO project and no Form. Inspect whether an Access As / object prefix is enforced on new tables or IDOs, whether the IDO Projects form shows a naming rule, whether the Multi-Site option exists, and whether the IDO Wizard leaves IDOs checked out. Prefer the core maintenance forms when they are available. Observe UI state through supported rendered interactions only. Capture decisive read-only evidence in evidence/EXP-038/ and write the initial experiment record. Do not create, edit, Save, Finish, delete, or generate any Mongoose object in T1. If a permission, session, wizard, or metadata error prevents establishing a safe supported path, record the blocker and stop without a workaround. Report the proposed single creation route, exact prerequisites, permissions, target-name absence, evidence paths, and whether mutation can safely be authorized in a separate task. Preserve the one-fresh-snapshot and one-corrected-inspection recovery limits throughout the experiment.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-093704-fZNX. Rationale: EXP-037 established that a custom Form event and Prompt handler can be saved and recovered in this tenant, but the factory has not yet established permission or a supported procedure for creating its own SQL table and IDO. The operator has authorized FX_-prefixed SQL tables and IDOs in the demo tenant. The smallest useful next step toward the Hello World tutorial is to establish whether the Site Developer user can create one minimal table-to-IDO pair without creating a Form. EXP-036-R2 also demonstrated that a Form wizard can fail with a ComponentFlags error, so the experiment must inspect available creation surfaces before mutation and stop at the first unsupported operation. Successful creation must be classified as observed, not replay_verified. | Operator review: record paths aligned, exact-value and no-JavaScript guards added. Standard Designer/Web Client lessons apply (select a tab before acting on it; ExtJS checkboxes toggle via their visible label; comboboxes take a literal value plus Enter). Specialist review (Infor CloudSuite Assistant, 2026-10-10) applied: IDO project is mandatory; project names may be alphanumeric-only (fallback FXHelloWorld01 as an operator-authorized naming exception); an enforced Access As prefix stops the run before mutation; Multi-Site cleared; check the new IDO in if left checked out. Operator: tenant-wide objects are acceptable in this demo development tenant. Approved by the operator 2026-10-10, including the FXHelloWorld01 fallback naming exception.
